body: Tuesday, July 07 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed remains in a holding pattern with a July decision imminent. Front-end yields are climbing — US 10Y at 4.52 (−1 bps vs 4W) and 2Y at 4.13 (prior close, +8 bps vs 4W) — indicating the market is repricing hawkish. The curve spread at +35 bps is positive but still flat, and the bear flattening via short-end repricing higher signals the market is abandoning near-term cut hopes. VIX at 15.77 (↓26.7% vs 4W) sits in complacency territory, a notable divergence from rising front-end yields.

New / Most Important: The payrolls data last week cooled — the dollar slid from a 13-month high as cooling payrolls shifted the rate outlook, and the DXY pulled back. Trump Accounts program is a new structural flow: CNBC reported on the potential for equity inflows from the new government savings program. Amazon readied a $25 billion bond deal, the largest single AI-linked corporate issuance signal this cycle. SpaceX joined the Nasdaq 100, which is structurally significant — this is a private-to-public transition event that reshuffles passive fund allocations and forces index-tracking capital (~$2T+ benchmarked to NDX) into a rocket/defense/satellite name, diluting pure-tech exposure in the index. Samsung and DeepSeek sparked a chip sell-off, dragging the Nasdaq on Monday. BofA flagged AI spending reaching $1.5 trillion, a figure that now anchors the capex cycle narrative. Goldman is pushing asset-heavy "HALO" trades, a clear pivot from the asset-light growth playbook that dominated 2020-2024.

Playbook ✓: Equity breadth expanding — Russell 2000 at 2996.58 (↑5.8% vs 4W) is outperforming Nasdaq 100 (↑1.3%), exactly what the rotation-into-value script predicts when yields rise. S&P 500 at 7519 (↑1.8%) grinding higher in low-vol regime.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: VIX at 15.77 amid rising yields and a major semiconductor sell-off is anomalous. The complacency regime persisting while the 2Y yield rises 8 bps in four weeks suggests equity markets are either right that the Fed is done, or deeply mispricing duration risk. The Goldman "HALO" call for asset-heavy outperformance is a structural break from the intangible-asset premium that drove returns for a decade. If capex-heavy companies (utilities, industrials, infrastructure) genuinely lead, it rewires factor exposure across every systematic strategy. This is a capital-flow story: money moves from momentum/growth into tangible-asset proxies, and it means the marginal dollar of AI spending accrues to builders, not software.

Macro Stance: The ECB raised rates in June — a hawkish surprise confirmed by ECB's Moulin stating the central bank is now in a "good position." Euro holds above 1.14 against the dollar. Eurozone inflation fell more than expected, yet the ECB still hiked, prioritizing credibility and wage persistence over headline deceleration. Panetta warned that Europe's defense spending surge could compromise central bank independence — a fiscal dominance flag.

New / Most Important: The ECB's June hike is the structural story. This is a central bank that was expected by many to be in an easing cycle by mid-2026, and instead it tightened. The Panetta warning is the real signal: European defense bills (driven by NATO rearmament, Greenland tensions, Turkey/Erdogan geopolitics all trending on X) are creating fiscal expansion that the ECB must accommodate or fight. This is a classic fiscal-monetary collision. If defense spending becomes a multi-year structural commitment, the ECB's terminal rate recalculates higher, EUR strengthens, and European duration gets repriced. Marine Le Pen trending on X alongside Farage and Clacton suggests political fragmentation risk remains elevated across the continent.

Playbook ✓: Euro holding firm post-hike, defense names bid.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Inflation falling while the ECB hikes is the divergence — this is preemptive tightening driven by fiscal outlook rather than current inflation data, a rare posture for the ECB and one that historically precedes policy errors.

Macro Stance: The PBOC is easing through volume while wary of the bond rally. It held the 7-day reverse repo rate while adding liquidity (TradingView, [Jun 30]) and ran a trillion-yuan outright reverse repo, ending a three-month tapering streak (BigGo Finance, [Jul 3]), but cut bond purchases on concern over falling yields (Bloomberg, [Jul 2]). The fixing leans against weakness: USD/CNY was set at 6.8047 versus 6.8088 (tmgm.com, [Jul 3]), a firmer-than-estimated fix that VT Markets reads as managed yuan strength amid softer growth ([Jul 3]); JPMorgan Asset Management bets the strong-yuan trend will flip (Bloomberg, [Jul 6]). Prices stay split: May CPI rose only 1.2% (China Daily, [Jun 10]) while factory-gate inflation hit a near four-year high (Reuters, [Jun 9]).

PMIs & Activity: June confirms an export- and tech-led upturn. The official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.3 and non-manufacturing to 50.2 (Reuters, [Jun 29]); the private factory gauge capped its strongest quarter since late 2020 (Reuters, [Jun 30]) though it grew less than expected (Bloomberg, [Jun 30]), and private services slowed slightly (Reuters, [Jul 2]). May showed the split: exports jumped 19.4% (AP News, [Jun 9]) while retail sales fell 0.6% (Il Sole 24 Ore, [Jun 15]) and fixed-asset investment was down 4.1% in the first five months (Macau Business, [Jun 16]). The domestic leg is still softening: NEV retail sales fell 7% in June on preliminary CPCA data (CnEVPost, [Jul 3]) as the subsidy pullback hits autos and appliances (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 2]), and a Nikkei survey sees second-quarter growth slowing on weak domestic demand ([Jul 6]).

Credit Impulse: The last print is two-track. Total social financing grew 7.7% in May (CGTN, [Jun 12]) and topped forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jun 12]), but new loans missed as the property slump curbed demand (Reuters, [Jun 12]). The beat is government bonds; Goldman's shorthand is that households are lying flat and no longer borrowing (Binance, [Jul 5]). Stress is surfacing in small lenders: Beijing took over Zhongbang Bank citing credit risks (The Standard, [Jul 3]), and the SCMP warns the rescue "might not be the last" ([Jul 6]) as the new top regulator steps up its risk cleanup (Bloomberg, [Jul 6]). Capping LGFV bond yields (IFR, [Jul 2]) keeps local funding cheap but does nothing for loan demand.

Property: Resale home prices fell faster in June, a private survey shows (Reuters, [Jun 30]), after new home prices fell at a faster pace in May (Reuters, [Jun 15]) and real-estate investment dropped 16.2% y/y in January–May (GMK Center, [Jun 18]). Sales are concentrating, not recovering: the top 100 developers sold nearly RMB 1.6 trillion in the first half with an 11.8% month-on-month rise in June (Moomoo, [Jul 1]), led by top-tier cities (Caixin, [Jul 3]), while Asia Times describes a market in free fall as buyers wait for floor prices ([Jul 3]). Restructuring runs under state direction: Country Garden cleared its first offshore coupon after its overhaul (Caixin, [Jul 2]) and Vanke named a former Shenzhen financial regulator as president (Caixin, [Jul 3]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Xi's growth pledge lifted stocks after the PMI (Modern Diplomacy, [Jul 1]), but consumer support is being withdrawn: tax breaks for energy-saving cars and NEVs are ending (chinadailyhk, [Jul 4]). Trade is thawing with Washington and hardening elsewhere. Beijing pledged $17 billion in annual US farm purchases (BigGo Finance, [Jul 2]) and will drop its 10% tariff on US agricultural goods (AgWeb, [Jul 6]); von der Leyen says the EU will retaliate if China misses the October deadline (Euronews, [Jul 3]), even as China signals openness to cutting the gap (SCMP, [Jul 3]). Beijing put export controls on 40 Japanese entities (AP News, [Jul 1]) and its state iron-ore buyer extended curbs on Fortescue (Bloomberg, [Jul 3]).

Markets & Flows: China is breaking step with global markets as investors buy in (Reuters, [Jul 6]), and the SCMP reads the divergent market as a microcosm of the economy ([Jul 6]). After an 11% first-half fall in Hong Kong (SCMP, [Jun 30]), mainland investors are buying SMIC and Zhipu AI (SCMP, [Jul 3]), foreign A-share holdings hit a record (Global Times, [Jul 1]) and China Resources New Energy tripled on debut (Business Times, [Jul 2]). The counter-signal is households: China's biggest ETF is now a US$13 billion gold fund as state stock-market support fades (Business Times, [Jul 6]).

New / Most Important: The "China breaks step" story is the key signal. While global equities face semiconductor headwinds and rising yields, Chinese equities are attracting inflows on a relative-value basis, and DeepSeek's role in the US chip sell-off reinforces China's AI-independence narrative. But the bid is narrow — AI, chips and new listings — and the PMI upturn behind it rests on tech exports, while property, private credit and car sales still deteriorate. This is a capital-flow rotation, not a reflation trade.

Playbook ✓: Easing through liquidity operations, a managed firm fixing and an AI-led equity bid are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The flows are running ahead of the growth pulse. An export-driven PMI at 50.3, a loan book households will not use and resale prices falling faster in June mean the rally prices an AI premium, not a domestic recovery, and the transmission follows that split. Construction demand stays weak, so iron ore is flat near $98 (Kalkine, [Jul 6]) and the AUD bounce lacks conviction (FOREX.com, [Jul 5]). European exporters take the other side: Goldman says Europe's growth is hit more by Chinese exports than by the bigger trade gap (Reuters, [Jul 2]). EM Asia gets AI flows but no demand impulse. Until loan growth and property sales outside the top tier turn, this is selective positioning, not macro confidence.

Macro Stance: The yen crisis is intensifying. USD/JPY at 162 — the market is calling Tokyo's bluff. The BOJ is under acute pressure from multiple directions: a sinking yen, robust economic data, government panel members calling for moderate hikes, and QT already underway (BOJ shed 15.6% of its massive assets per Wolf Street). Yet the BOJ's slow, dovish leadership revamp casts doubt on whether hikes will actually materialize at pace.

New / Most Important: This is the most structurally important story in global macro right now. USD/JPY at 162 represents a yen that has blown through every level the market assumed would trigger intervention or accelerated tightening. The BOJ is attempting QT as a substitute for rate hikes — shedding balance sheet rather than raising the policy rate — but the market is not accepting this as sufficient. Japan wage growth missed, clouding the hike outlook and keeping the yen under pressure. This is a carry-trade supercycle feedback loop: weak yen → capital outflows → weaker yen → BOJ credibility erodes → more carry selling. The headline "BOJ's First Rate Hike in 31 Years Gains Momentum" tells you how far behind the curve they are. Korean stocks flirting with bear territory are collateral damage from the yen — competitive devaluation pressure spreading across Asia. The Nikkei dropped on semiconductor earnings jitters, adding an equity-side headwind to the currency crisis. If the BOJ actually hikes into a semi downturn, the carry unwind could be violent and globally systemic.

Playbook ✓: Yen weakness forcing BOJ's hand — this has been the base case for a year.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The BOJ choosing QT over rate hikes is the divergence — no major central bank has tried to defend its currency primarily through balance sheet reduction while keeping rates near zero. It isn't working.

Macro Stance: Australia now tops inflation rankings among all major developed economies. Economists are calling for no rate cuts until 2027 and flagging a fourth hike as a live possibility. The RBA has been described as having "failed" on inflation.

New / Most Important: This is a structural break from the "synchronized global easing" narrative. Australia being the worst inflation performer in the developed world while simultaneously facing housing affordability conditions worse than the 17% rate era is a policy trap. If the RBA hikes again, it risks a housing crash in a market where household leverage is among the highest globally. If it doesn't, inflation persistence damages credibility and the AUD. This is a no-win setup — the kind of environment where you short the currency and short the banks simultaneously.

Playbook ✓: Sticky services inflation keeping the RBA hawkish — on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The market pricing no cuts until 2027 is the divergence — this was supposed to be a 2025 easing story. Australia is now an outlier in the developed world, and capital flows will reflect that via AUD weakness and bank equity underperformance.

Macro Stance: The RPP decides this week (Strefa Inwestorów, [Jul 7]) and nobody expects a move: wnp.pl reports a large bank has no doubts about the outcome [Jul 7], and Gazeta Prawna's line is a July hold with cuts a 2027 question [Jul 6]. Bankier.pl frames the real event as the July inflation projection rather than the rate itself [Jul 7]. The setup is the June GUS flash at 2.5% y/y, back at the NBP target and below forecasts (Parkiet, [Jun 30]), after which Commerzbank noted that rate hike bets have vanished and ING flagged a market starting to play for cuts in the second half of 2026 [Jun 30], all of which has kept the zloty capped amid mixed data. The counterweights are the end of the CPN fuel package, which Gazeta Prawna warned could push inflation toward 3% [Jun 30], and energy costs that WP Wiadomości says are hitting industry and threatening jobs and competitiveness [Jul 7]. The manufacturing PMI dropped to 46.1 in June versus a 49.4 consensus (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 1]), though German industry is rebounding (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 7]). Labour is the strong leg: GUS counts 1.1 mn foreigners working in Poland (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 7]).

Markets: Tuesday was a rotation session: CD Projekt led gains while KGHM fell the most (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 7]), Allegro and Żabka defended an index that closed slightly lower (DlaHandlu.pl, [Jul 7]), and FXMAG recorded Modivo +4.59% and LPP +1.99% while Samsung dropped over 10% and the KOSPI lost 7% [Jul 7]. KGHM's slide is a verdict on Strategy 2055+: FXMAG says the shares plunged [Jul 7] and INNPoland.pl reports the company's largest-ever investment programme failed to convince analysts [Jul 7]; the card still shows 328.55 (+2.4% 1W, -3.4% 4W) on Monday's close. Banks face their own valuation question, with pb.pl reporting analysts now consider GPW bank shares too expensive, citing a long list of risk factors [Jul 7], even as PKO closed 105.82 (+2.4% 1W, +6.6% 4W) and Pekao 234.8 (+3.2% 1W, 0.0% 4W). Elsewhere on the card: Orlen 133.5 (+6.8% 1W, -7.8% 4W), Allegro 38.8 (+4.5% 1W, +12.6% 4W), CD Projekt 233.3 (+5.5% 1W, +2.7% 4W), LPP 18,920 (+2.3% 1W, -12.9% 4W), PGE 9.44 (-0.3% 1W, -7.3% 4W) and Dino 27.76 (-5.2% 1W, -5.9% 4W) at its lowest since 2022 after the Barclays recommendation (XTB.com, [Jul 3]). EPOL closed 39.9 (+4.3% 1W, -1.1% 4W). The zloty is drifting: EUR/PLN stays close to 4.29 (FXMAG, [Jul 7]) in what Bankier.pl calls a sideways range, with the pound at its most expensive in over a year [Jul 7];  Card: USD/PLN 3.7457 (-0.2% 1W, +1.9% 4W), EUR/PLN 4.2861 (flat 1W, +1.1% 4W). POLGBs: investors bought Polish bonds worth billions in May (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 3]).

Fiscal & Politics: Defence money is reshaping the fiscal debate. The finance ministry published calculations showing Poland will save billions through the EU's SAFE loans (Next Gazeta.pl, [Jul 7]), Business Insider Polska reports those loans are feeding the Polish army [Jul 7], and PKO BP estimates that defence modernisation could generate a 1.3 trn zł demand impulse by 2035 (Forsal.pl, [Jul 7]). Deregulation 2.0, presented by Berek and Domański with more than a dozen tax changes for 2027 (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 6]), is paired with a less welcome item: Gazeta Prawna says a new tax from 2027 will surprise savers because no profit is needed to owe it [Jul 7], and Business Insider Polska reads the OKI law as the Sejm forcing Poles to invest from 2027 [Jul 7]. The CPN fuel package has ended, and Interia Biznes reports the minister disclosing when it could return [Jul 7], while the windfall tax on fuel companies is meant to cover its 4 bn zł cost (Biznes Wprost, [Jul 2]).

Corporate & Sectors: Orlen placed 750 mn euro of green eurobonds with demand more than twice the offer (Strefa Inwestorów, [Jul 7]), wnp.pl notes it is now larger than Rosneft and every Russian oil company [Jul 7], and Rzeczpospolita sees a chance of cheaper Norwegian gas with the market already pricing part of the benefit [Jul 7]. KGHM's plan, over 32 bn zł and new mines (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 7]), is being sold rather than bought. PGE: Rzeczpospolita says the Turów dispute is not over and a key decision still lies ahead [Jul 7], and customers are waiting months for invoices under a new billing system (Spider's Web, [Jul 7]). PKO BP joined NATO's initiative to draw private capital into defence (Money.pl, [Jul 7]), while mBank's new offer was described as a flop (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 7]). LPP's Sinsay reached 2.5 thousand stores after opening 500 in the half (PropertyNews.pl, [Jul 7]). Dino faces an approaching general strike (mamNewsa, [Jul 7]), and the finance ministry has named the date WIBOR disappears for borrowers (Bankier.pl, [Jul 5]).

Geopolitics & Security: The Poland-Ukraine rift widened: Budanov said Ukraine will not accept ultimatums from Poland (Euromaidan Press, [Jul 7]), Gazeta Prawna reports Ukraine asking for Patriot missiles with the Netherlands saying it has exhausted its capacity [Jul 7], and The Times of India wrote of Tusk's warning to his own president amid the tussle with Zelensky [Jul 7]. Sikorski again warned of a possible Russian provocation against Poland, citing trust in US guarantees (polskieradio.pl, [Jul 7]), after the US warning of an armed test of NATO on Polish territory (The Telegraph, [Jul 3]). Poland and NATO allies struck a deal to build Europe's first PAC-3 missile centre (TVP World, [Jul 7]).

New / Most Important: The collapse in hike expectations is the story. Poland went from hike-pricing to neutral in a single data cycle, and the decision is now a non-event: what matters is whether the projection validates 2027 cuts or pushes them out on fuel. The market has meanwhile started differentiating: KGHM is punished for capex, banks are being called expensive, and Allegro and CD Projekt carry the index.  |  Playbook ✓: CEE FX range-bound amid mixed data; EUR/PLN pinned near 4.29 into the decision is exactly the script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: A 1.3 trn zł defence impulse financed by EU loans is a growth story the PMI at 46.1 does not yet show; if the gap persists, the fiscal cost arrives before the demand.

Macro Stance: Turkey and Egypt are dominating X trending — Erdogan, geopolitical tensions, and the Argentina-Egypt match driving attention. Vietnam is pursuing capital market reforms and targeting a global index upgrade, a structural flow catalyst.

New / Most Important: Vietnam's upgrade ambitions are the actionable signal. An MSCI or FTSE upgrade from frontier to emerging would force billions in passive reallocation. Turkey/Egypt trending appears geopolitical (NATO, Greenland tensions, regional realignment) rather than financial.  |  Playbook ✓: EM currencies muted as dollar holds firm.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The Indian rupee slipping to a two-week low as US Treasury yields surge is notable — INR is more rate-sensitive than consensus assumes.

Narrative: Mixed: AI capex is still the anchor thesis — BofA cites $1.5T in potential AI spending — but a chip sell-off dragged the Nasdaq lower and money is rotating from software platforms to physical-infrastructure builders, with the hyperscalers "falling behind in the AI trade".

Reported: Progress Software's Q2 earnings and revenue surpassed estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 30]) and it raised its outlook on AI demand (TradingView, [Jul 1]), sending the stock skyrocketing (The Motley Fool, [Jul 1]). UK public-sector IT supplier Made Tech delivered strong earnings growth as AI-driven demand accelerates (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jun 30]).

EPS Upside Watch: BILL Holdings — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 2]), the cleanest signal of a coming beat. Celestica — the AI-hardware contract manufacturer is rated a buy ahead of earnings (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 1]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hyperscalers underperforming is structurally new: Goldman's asset-heavy "HALO" trade inverts the asset-light premium that drove tech leadership for a decade. If AI value accrues to capex deployers — data centres, power, chips — rather than platform owners, XLK leadership redraws toward industrials-adjacent names.

Narrative: Mixed: the market is re-categorising communication platforms as AI-infrastructure plays — Meta is now framed as a "neocloud" against Nebius — so AI capex, not the ad cycle, now sets the multiple.
Reported: No major reports this week.
EPS Upside Watch: SoftBank — Citi raised its target on profit growth (Yahoo Finance Australia, [Jun 30]). LBG Media — Berenberg slightly raised its target price (Sharecast.com, [Jul 1]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Platform power cuts both ways: the LadBible boss calls the traffic hit from Meta's feed shake-up a 'tough pill to swallow' (The Guardian, [Jul 5]). Publishers that live on social referrals carry earnings risk that the platforms themselves do not.

Narrative: Bullish, but only modestly: the 10Y at 4.52 (−1 bps vs 4W) and the 2Y at 4.13 (+8 bps) leave a positive yet flat +35 bps curve — modest NIM support, not textbook expansion — while the low VIX trims trading revenue but supports credit quality. Bank stocks are rallying ahead of earnings (Investor's Business Daily, [Jul 6]).

Reported: CMC Markets lifted guidance for full-year net operating income and the shares surged (Sharecast.com, [Jul 1]) as its B2B platform growth accelerates (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 1]). FactSet's Q3 earnings beat estimates on organic revenue growth (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 1]). HDFC Bank led Indian shares to a 10-week high after strong Q1 growth (Reuters, [Jul 6]).

EPS Upside Watch: Robinhood — its business momentum may be outrunning earnings estimates (Zacks Investment Research, [Jul 6]). American Express — gains momentum as analysts raise price targets (Blockonomi, [Jul 5]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The analyst who loved bank stocks for 15 years just flipped (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 1]) — a contrarian warning just as the group rallies into the Q2 season on a curve that is still flat.

Narrative: Bearish: WTI at 70.46 (↓22.2% vs 4W) is a violent decline, and the growth pulse shows no demand collapse (US ISM manufacturing is still expanding and China's official PMI rose to 50.3), so the drop points to supply — OPEC+ boosting output — more than to demand destruction.

Reported: Shell signalled a strong oil and gas trading profit on the Iran war (Yahoo Finance Singapore, [Jul 6]). Nigeria's NNPC said profit fell to ₦462 billion despite higher oil production in May (Premium Times Nigeria, [Jul 2]).

EPS Upside Watch: PBF Energy — surging earnings estimates signal upside for the refiner (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 30]). Patterson-UTI — analysts raised their earnings views on the driller (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 3]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Big Oil heads for record profits even as Trump turns up the heat on gas prices (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 6]), with WTI down 22.2% in four weeks. Trading gains flatter the coming prints, so the bear case will show up in guidance rather than in reported results.

Narrative: Bullish: Goldman's asset-heavy "HALO" trade directly favours industrials, NATO defence spending and SpaceX's ascent feed the aerospace and defence complex, and cheaper fuel (WTI ↓22.2%) feeds through to transport margins.

Reported: Maersk sharply raised 2026 guidance on stronger-than-expected container demand and rising spot freight rates (iMarine, [Jul 2]). MSC Industrial beat on price gains and volume growth (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 2]). Shipowner Norden raised its 2026 full-year net profit guidance (Baird Maritime, [Jul 2]).

EPS Upside Watch: Delta Air Lines — reports on July 10 with the Street expecting $1.48 EPS (AlphaStreet, [Jul 6]), and the stock is near highs with oil below $70 (Investor's Business Daily, [Jul 2]) — fuel savings drop to margins. Sats — analysts raised target prices on a cargo recovery (The Business Times, [Jul 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: IATA still expects airline profits to halve in 2026 (The Edge Malaysia, [Jul 1]): if cheap fuel is not yet in the industry forecasts, Q2 airline prints are where the upside surprise shows first.

Narrative: Mixed: tariff pass-through is hitting consumer electronics — Best Buy and Apple flagged a "price shock for shoppers" — and Walmart cutting prices to win inflation-weary Americans signals stress at the margin, with cheaper fuel (WTI ↓22.2%) the offset.

Reported: Nike beat by $0.08 and topped revenue estimates (Investing.com, [Jun 30]) but flagged a prolonged turnaround as the China slump and a weak outlook eclipsed the beat (Reuters, [Jul 1]). Tesla's Q2 deliveries beat forecasts (Fox Business, [Jul 2]), yet the stock sank 7% (CNBC, [Jul 2]). Sodexo raised its full-year organic revenue growth forecast on a strong quarter (Reuters, [Jul 2]).
EPS Upside Watch: Rivian — raised its 2026 delivery outlook (CNBC, [Jul 2]), and JPMorgan raised its target after strong Q2 deliveries (TradingView, [Jul 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Apple "weathering" hardware price increases while Best Buy flags a price shock is a bifurcation: brand pricing power is diverging from commodity retail — a tale of two consumers.

Narrative: Mixed: defensives should benefit from rising front-end yields and semiconductor volatility, but the VIX at 15.77 shows no panic rotation yet, and big-box price cuts are deflationary for the sector's pricing power.

Reported: General Mills beat Q4 estimates with organic sales flat y/y (TradingView, [Jul 1]) and jumped 9.9% as it sees up to $3 billion in savings (TradingView, [Jul 2]). Constellation Brands' Q1 revenue fell 3.3% (Quartz, [Jul 3]), yet the stock rose (Barron's, [Jun 30]). AB Foods led FTSE declines on a sugar warning and mixed Primark sales (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jun 30]).
EPS Upside Watch: Coca-Cola — a fourth consecutive earnings beat sets up a run toward a new high (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 3]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: General Mills says fiscal '27 will be a better year (Food Business News, [Jul 2]) while it chases thrifty consumers with protein and pet food (WSJ, [Jul 1]): cost cuts, not volume, are carrying staples earnings.

Narrative: Mixed: healthcare is quiet in the flow data — Pfizer's attention on X looks political or regulatory rather than pipeline-driven — and with the 10Y at 4.52 the group lacks a rate tailwind, while the VIX at 15.77 shows no defensive rotation yet. Q2 previews are where the signal is now.

Reported: Craneware, the UK healthcare software group, slumped after slower conversion triggered a profit warning (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 3]). Elite Pharmaceuticals' Q4 call highlighted record revenue growth (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 30]).

EPS Upside Watch: UnitedHealth — Morgan Stanley raised its price target ahead of Q2 earnings (TIKR.com, [Jul 1]). Johnson & Johnson — its MedTech segment eyes another strong quarter in Q2 (The Globe and Mail, [Jul 6]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Device makers are guiding up while drug pricing stays political: Medtronic is betting on new devices and $1.5B in acquisitions to grow its value (Twin Cities Business, [Jul 6]), a volume story that does not depend on Washington.

Narrative: Bearish: copper at 6.22 (↓0.6% vs 4W) now trades as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal and tracks the chip sell-off, gold at 4156 (↓4.2%) is pulling back, and China's property data — resale prices falling faster in June, real-estate investment down 16.2% y/y in January–May — offers no construction catalyst.
Reported: No major reports this week.

EPS Upside Watch: Nickel Industries — its price target was raised and the analyst remains bullish (TheBull.com.au, [Jul 2]). Chinese chemical makers — mid-year forecasts project earnings growth as high as 952%, with positive preliminary results (Moomoo, [Jul 4]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver near $58 is outperforming gold on industrial demand from solar and AI hardware — the white metals are trading as technology inputs while the rest of the materials tape stays weak.

Narrative: Bearish: the 10Y at 4.52 (−1 bps vs 4W) remains a direct headwind for cap rates, and Australian housing analysis showing conditions worse than in the 17% rate era underscores global real-estate stress.
Reported: No major reports this week.
